price_note: About $40 weekend walking, cart about $23 extra; senior rate about $30 (listings conflict).
notes: City-owned course. Carts are extra (about $23 per person in public listings).

price_note: Roughly $130-140 on weekends, cart included (reviewer and listing reports; call to confirm).
terrain_note: Tom Fazio design (2001) along the Housatonic River; undulating parkland, reviewers mention several slopes to climb.
notes: One of the hardest public tests in CT from the back tees (slope about 146-152). Wind off the river; at least one reviewer mentions a carry over marsh.

price_note: Listings range from about $30 to $79 for 18 holes; call to confirm.
notes: Family-owned Geoffrey Cornish layout, open year-round. Reviewers mention good pace of play.

price_note: About $51 weekend green fee; about $74 with cart on GolfNow deals.
terrain_note: Rolling fairways lined with large trees.
notes: Geoffrey Cornish design (1969); long from the back tees.

price_note: Jones about $69 and Player about $65 on weekends; the Apple Nine is about $16.
terrain_note: Front nine has dramatically rolling hills; back nine is flatter, through woods and wetlands with some water and a covered bridge. Routed through the orchards over gently rolling hills.
notes: Three courses: Jones (hilly front nine), Player (gently rolling), and the short Apple Nine. Robert Trent Jones Sr. design (1969). Gary Player design (1994). Over 30 bunkers around small greens; reviewers call it more target golf. Short 9-hole course (2012): seven par 3s and two par 4s. Good for beginners and short-game practice.

price_note: $60 for 18 holes on weekends (2025 town rate sheet); senior ID discounts on weekdays.
notes: Town course (1976). Slope from the back tees about 125-133.

price_note: $23 for 9 holes on weekends (2025 town rate sheet).
notes: Short executive nine next to Tashua Knolls; listed as the easiest course in Fairfield County by slope on one site.

price_note: About $39 on weekends for 18 holes (listing); GolfNow deals around $26-33.
terrain_note: Mostly flat and open, but one reviewer says holes 1, 9, 10 and 18 are very hilly. Winding hills with scenic views; reviewers agree it is hillier and harder than the Red.
notes: Two courses: the Red (more open and forgiving) and the Black (hillier). City of Bridgeport course. More forgiving and open than the Black; popular with beginners and casual golfers. Championship-style municipal course.

price_note: About $54 on weekends for 18 holes (listing); call for current rates.
terrain_note: Views of the trap-rock ridges and Castle Craig.
notes: City course (1933). Water hazards and many bunkers. Gold tees about 5,783 yards.

price_note: About $16-22 for 9 par-3 holes; resident discounts.
terrain_note: Links-style par 3 course near the water.
notes: Nine par 3s, mostly short (a couple under 100 yards, one about 200). Very beginner-friendly and inexpensive.

price_note: About $104 on weekends, cart included (Chronogolf average).
terrain_note: 530 acres of rolling hills and forest with elevation changes on many holes; the 4th is a 202-yard par 3 with a big drop.
notes: Upscale public course; reviewers describe it as very hilly to walk. Rocks, streams and stone walls.

price_note: About $53 on weekends for 18 holes (listing); about $70 with cart.
notes: Shorter 18 (about 5,800 yards from the tips), walking allowed. Geoffrey Cornish design (1967). Reviewers call the 9th one of the toughest par 3s in the state.
